title: What Muslims Believe in One God: A Simple Introduction to the Basic Idea of God in Islam
summary: Islam teaches that there is only one God who created everything and watches over everyone. Muslims believe God is loving, merciful, and fair. He has no partners, no children, and nothing is equal to Him.

sections.title: Tawheed Before You Were Born: The Primordial Covenant
sections.content: When Allah took the covenant from the backs of Adam’s children: “Am I not your Lord?” every soul answered “Yes, we testify” (7:172). Tawheed is not something you learn — it is something you remember. This covenant (Mithaq) is etched in every human heart, and life is a journey to revive that innate fitrah before the soul returns to answer the same question again.

deepDive.title: The Fitrah of Creation
deepDive.content: Children are born upon fitrah (natural inclination to Tawheed), as confirmed by the Prophet ﷺ. Shaytan’s lifelong mission is to make you forget this covenant, replacing it with shirk that veils the heart like rust on iron.

sections.title: The Three Categories of Tawheed (The Standard Framework)
sections.content:
1. Tawheed ar-Ruboobiyyah – Oneness of Lordship: Allah alone is the Creator, Sustainer, Provider, and Controller of all affairs. Even idol-worshippers of Makkah affirmed this, but it is incomplete without the other two.
  2. Tawheed al-Uloohiyyah (al-‘Ibadah) – Oneness of Worship: Directing all acts of devotion—prayer, dua, sacrifice, vow, fear, hope, trust, love—exclusively to Allah, without intermediaries.
  3. Tawheed al-Asmaa’ was-Sifaat – Oneness of Names and Attributes: Affirming Allah’s Names and Attributes as described in the Qur’an and Sunnah, without distortion, negation, likening to creation, or questioning 'how'.

deepDive.title: Why Three? The Qur’anic Balance
deepDive.content: These categories ensure comprehensive Tawheed: belief in Allah’s dominion (Ruboobiyyah), exclusive worship (Uloohiyyah), and perfect description (Asmaa’ wa Sifaat). Neglecting any leads to imbalance, as seen in the pagans who affirmed creation but directed worship elsewhere.

sections.title: Extended Discussions on Tawheed: Ittibaa’ and Beyond
sections.content: Some scholars, like Ibn Taymiyyah, discuss Tawheed al-Ittibaa’ (Oneness of Following) as integral to Uloohiyyah—complete submission to the Prophet’s Sunnah as the practical manifestation of worship. While not a separate 'fourth' category in the standard division, it emphasizes that true Tawheed requires emulating the Messenger ﷺ in every detail.

deepDive.title: Ittibaa’ in Action
deepDive.content: Following the Prophet ﷺ is obligatory: “Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah” (4:80). This includes Sunnah prayers, adab, and rulings—neglect here weakens overall Tawheed.

sections.title: The Greatest Ayah in the Qur’an: Ayat al-Kursi
sections.content: 2:255 summarises all categories of Tawheed in ten sentences. The Prophet ﷺ called it the leader of all verses. Reciting it three times morning and evening protects from Shaytan, as per authentic hadith.

deepDive.title: Breaking Down Ayat al-Kursi
deepDive.content: Verses 1-4: Ruboobiyyah (creation, knowledge). 5-6: Uloohiyyah (no sleep, protector). 7: Asmaa’ wa Sifaat (Owner of heavens/earth, no intercessor without permission).

sections.title: Tawheed of the Prophets in 60 Seconds Each
sections.content:
• Nuh → 950 years calling: “Worship Allah alone; you have no god but Him” (23:23).
  • Ibrahim → Smashed idols, built Ka’bah: “Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth” (6:79).
  • Musa → Confronted Pharaoh: “Let my people go that they may worship” (Exodus parallel in 7:127).
  • ‘Isa → Refuted divinity: “Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord” (5:116-117).
  • Muhammad ﷺ → Final call: “Say: La ilaha illa Allah and succeed” (Yasin 36:58-59).

deepDive.title: Common Thread
deepDive.content: Every prophet’s mission began and ended with Tawheed—proof that it is the unchanging core of divine message across 124,000 prophets.

sections.title: Tawheed in the Grave, on the Sirat, and at the Hawd
sections.content: Your Tawheed will be your light on the bridge (Sirat), the reason the Prophet ﷺ gives you a drink from his blessed hands (Hawd), and the only currency accepted on a Day when wealth and children avail nothing (26:88-89).

deepDive.title: The First Question
deepDive.content: Munkar and Nakir ask: “Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?” Tawheed answers all three perfectly.

sections.title: The Ten Nullifiers of Tawheed (Nawaqid al-Islam)
sections.content: As outlined by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abdil-Wahhab: 1. Shirk in worship. 2. Setting up intermediaries. 3. Not deeming polytheists as disbelievers. 4. Believing other guidance superior. 5. Hating the Prophet’s message. 6. Mocking Islam. 7. Practicing sorcery. 8. Aiding disbelievers against Muslims. 9. Believing exemption from Shari’ah. 10. Turning away from the religion.

deepDive.title: Modern Applications
deepDive.content: Today, this includes nationalism over Ummah, celebrity worship, or ignoring Sunnah—each a crack in Tawheed’s foundation.

sections.title: Hidden Shirk Checklist (Modern Edition)
sections.content:
• Showing off in worship (riya’)
  • Swearing by creation
  • Saying “If it weren’t for so-and-so…”
  • Fearing superstitions more than Allah
  • Relying on wealth/status over tawakkul
  • Seeking fatwas from unqualified sources
  • Nationalism eclipsing brotherhood
  • Delayed obedience to revelation

deepDive.title: Daily Audit
deepDive.content: End each day reviewing: Did any of these creep in? Repent immediately—shirk is the only unforgivable sin without tawbah (4:48).

sections.title: The Four Stages of Protecting Tawheed
sections.content:
1. Learn: Study sources deeply (Qur’an, authentic Sunnah).
  2. Live: Apply in every decision, big or small.
  3. Teach: Share with family, friends, online—da’wah preserves your own Tawheed.
  4. Die: Make dua for ikhlas in final moments; prepare with constant renewal.

deepDive.title: Renewal Practices
deepDive.content: Daily: Recite Shahada 100x. Weekly: Study one hadith on Tawheed. Monthly: Teach a lesson.

sections.title: Tawheed in Times of Trial: Stories from the Sahaba
sections.content: Bilal under torture screamed 'Ahad! Ahad!' (One! One!). Sumayyah martyred for refusing to deny Tawheed. Their hearts were fortresses—yours can be too.

title: The Beliefs: The Six Pillars of Iman, Your Invisible Reality Stronger Than Steel
summary: While the body lives in the seen world, the heart lives permanently in the unseen (ghayb). The six pillars of Iman are the oxygen of the soul — without them you suffocate spiritually even while walking around healthy. They transform abstract belief into a lived certainty that reshapes every decision.
learningObjectives: Map the six pillars of Iman onto everyday actions.
Recognize unseen realities (angels, books, prophets, qadar) that shape belief.

sections.title: The Branches of Iman: Over Seventy Levels of Excellence
sections.content: As per the hadith in Sahih Muslim: Iman has over seventy branches—the highest is La ilaha illa Allah, the lowest is removing harm from the road, and modesty (haya’) is a branch. Al-Bayhaqi compiled 77 in Shu’ab al-Iman, including lowering the gaze, helping the needy, and patience in trials.

deepDive.title: Iman Increases and Decreases
deepDive.content: Obedience elevates branches (e.g., charity strengthens trust in provision); sins prune them. Renew daily through dhikr and reflection.

sections.title: Belief in Allah – The Unshakable Core
sections.content: Affirming Tawheed in full, with balanced love, fear, hope, and reliance. This pillar underpins all others—weak here, and the rest crumbles.

sections.title: Living with Angels – Your Constant Companions
sections.content:
• Kiraman Katibin: Scribes on shoulders recording every deed.
  • Guardians: Hafazah protect from unseen harms.
  • Attendees of Dhikr: Angels descend on gatherings reciting Qur’an.
  • Amin-Sayers: Behind you in salah, amplifying supplication.
  • Throne-Bearers: Eight on Judgment Day, glorifying Allah eternally.

deepDive.title: Angelic Etiquette
deepDive.content: Angels flee from foul odors (garlic post-eating), love sweet scents, and pray for the sleeper who says adhkar. Honor them by purity.

sections.title: Belief in the Revealed Books – The Chain of Divine Guidance
sections.content: Allah revealed over 100 scriptures, but four principal books remain referenced: Suhuf (Scrolls) of Ibrahim, Tawrat (Torah) to Musa, Zabur (Psalms) to Dawud, Injil (Gospel) to ‘Isa, and the final, preserved Qur’an to Muhammad ﷺ. We believe in their originals, though previous ones were altered.

deepDive.title: The Qur’an’s Uniqueness
deepDive.content: Unlike others, the Qur’an is mutawatir (mass-transmitted), memorized by millions, and challenges: “Produce a surah like it” (2:23)—unmet for 1400 years.

sections.title: 25 Prophets Mentioned by Name – Quick Profiles of Guidance
sections.content: The Qur’an names 25 prophets (from 124,000 total, 313 messengers): 1. Adam (first human). 2. Idris (ascended). 3. Nuh (ark-builder, 950 years). 4. Hud (to ‘Ad). 5. Salih (she-camel). 6. Ibrahim (friend of Allah). 7. Lut (Sodom). 8. Isma’il (sacrifice). 9. Ishaq (laughter). 10. Ya’qub (Israel). 11. Yusuf (dreams). 12. Ayyub (patience). 13. Shu’ayb (Midyan). 14. Musa (9 signs). 15. Harun (orator). 16. Dhul-Kifl (patient judge). 17. Dawud (melody). 18. Sulayman (winds/jinn). 19. Ilyas (Baal-fighter). 20. Al-Yasa’ (successor). 21. Yunus (whale). 22. Zakariyya (old father). 23. Yahya (baptist). 24. ‘Isa (miracles). 25. Muhammad ﷺ (seal).

deepDive.title: Lessons from Each
deepDive.content: Adam: Repentance. Nuh: Perseverance. Yusuf: Forgiveness. Muhammad ﷺ: Mercy to all worlds.

sections.title: Detailed Stages of the Hereafter: From Barzakh to Eternity
sections.content: 1. Death (soul extraction). 2. Barzakh (grave life: garden or pit). 3. Signs of Hour (minor: e.g., women outnumber men; major: Dajjal, Mahdi). 4. Trumpet blow (Israfil). 5. Resurrection (bodies reformed). 6. Gathering (Mahshar: 50,000 years, sweating per sins). 7. Book of Deeds (right/left hand). 8. Reckoning (private judgment). 9. Scales (deeds weighed). 10. Sirat (bridge over Hell). 11. Hawd (Prophet’s pool). 12. Shafa’ah (intercession). 13. Araf (purgatory for major sinners). 14. Jannah (8 gates) or Jahannam (7 levels).

deepDive.title: Barzakh Realities
deepDive.content: The grave squeezes the believer gently (like a hug), expands for the righteous into Paradise vistas. Punishment for sinners: walls closing in, whispers of regret.

sections.title: Qadar in Four Simple Equations: Balancing Free Will and Decree
sections.content:
• Allah’s Knowledge: Eternal awareness of all.
  • Preserved Tablet: Written 50,000 years pre-creation.
  • Universal Will: Nothing occurs without permission.
  • Creation: Allah creates actions; we choose intentions.

deepDive.title: No Contradiction
deepDive.content: You feel free, so accountable; Allah’s justice ensures fairness. Response to calamity: “Qadr Allah, and He does what He wills” (18:39 partial).

sections.content: 1. Morning/evening adhkar. 2. Graveyard visits. 3. Tafsir reading. 4. Monday/Thursday fasts. 5. Sadaqah drops. 6. Death reflection. 7. Dua for yaqeen. 8. Prophet stories. 9. Qadar gratitude. 10. Unseen proofs journaling.

sections.content: Atheism, science, media—each tests Iman. Anchor in Qur’an: “We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves” (41:53). Miracles abound for the seeking heart.

title: The Pillars: The Five Pillars, Your Direct Phone Line to Allah
summary: These five actions are the bare minimum Allah asks in return for Jannah. They are gifts wrapped as obligations. Miss them and everything else collapses; perfect them and every nafl act becomes mountains of reward. The Prophet ﷺ called them the 'framework of Islam'—build your life upon them.

sections.title: Shahada – The Key That Never Rusts
sections.content: Renew it every prayer, every adhan, every time you sneeze, every time you enter the toilet, every time you feel doubt. It’s the door to all other pillars.

deepDive.title: Seven Conditions Revisited
deepDive.content: Knowledge, certainty, acceptance, submission, truthfulness, sincerity, love—fulfill these, and Shahada becomes your eternal shield.

sections.title: Salah – 50→5 Gift of the Night Journey
sections.content: The only obligation brought directly (not via Jibril) during Mi’raj. The Prophet ﷺ kept going back until reduced to 5 with reward of 50. Includes 17 fard rak’ahs + 12 rawatib sunnahs daily.

deepDive.title: The 12 Daily Sunnah Prayers (Rawatib)
deepDive.content: 2 before Fajr, 4+2 before/after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha = house in Paradise (Bukhari). Prioritize for exponential reward.

sections.title: Zakat – Financial Detox and Social Justice
sections.content: Obligatory 2.5% on idle wealth (cash, gold, silver, investments) after one lunar year above nisab. For 2025: Nisab ≈ $6,000 (87.48g gold) or $1,100 (612.36g silver, per Hanafi). Eight recipients (9:60): poor, needy, administrators, etc.

deepDive.title: Voluntary Sadaqah Multiplier
deepDive.content: Zakat purifies; sadaqah multiplies up to 700x. Even a smile is charity—circulate wealth to circulate barakah.

sections.title: Sawm – Training the Soul for 11 Months
sections.content: Controls tongue, eyes, stomach, desires from true dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib). The fast is for Me and I reward it (without measure) — Allah Himself is the direct reward (Hadith Qudsi).

deepDive.title: Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr)
deepDive.content: Worship equals 83+ years. Prophet ﷺ sought it in last 10 nights via i’tikaf—emulate for forgiveness of prior/current years.

sections.title: Hajj – Standing Where the Prophets Stood
sections.content: Once in lifetime if able: Ihram (intention), Tawaf (circling Ka’bah), Sa’i (between Safa-Marwah), Arafah (standing in supplication), Muzdalifah (pebbles), Rami (stoning), Sacrifice (Eid), Tawaf Ifadah. Every prophet performed it.

deepDive.title: Arafah: The Pillar of Pillars
deepDive.content: Best dua day: “La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah…” Fasting Arafah expiates two years’ sins.

sections.title: No Sixth Pillar: Clarifying Misconceptions
sections.content: Islam has exactly five pillars per authentic hadith. Some fringe groups (e.g., Kharijites) added jihad, but scholars reject this—jihad is fard kifayah (communal), not individual like pillars. Walā’ & Barā’ (loyalty/disavowal) is aqeedah, not a pillar.

deepDive.title: Jihad’s True Place
deepDive.content: The greater jihad is against nafs (self); lesser is defense. Pillars are personal; focus here first.

sections.title: Daily, Weekly, Yearly, Lifetime Checklist: Building Rhythm
sections.content:
• Daily: 5 fard + rawatib + witr.
  • Weekly: Jumu’ah with khutbah.
  • Yearly: Ramadan fast + Zakat due.
  • Lifetime: Hajj/Umrah.

deepDive.title: Eid Connections
deepDive.content: Eid al-Fitr (post-Ramadan), Eid al-Adha (with Hajj)—celebrations tying pillars together in joy and gratitude.

sections.title: The Fruits of the Pillars: Transformation Stories
sections.content: Abu Bakr’s salah softened hearts; Umar’s fasting tamed his anger; companions’ zakat ended famines—your consistency can change generations.
